places.name: Hàn Giao Chử
places.size: A low black-rock islet about 800 m long in the sea, ringed by a coiling ridge of pressure ice and a frozen skirt about 2 km across. The outer gate of a great sect: about 20 buildings (stables, three halls, an alchemist's hall outside the wall) inside a 200 m wall, with perhaps 40 stewards and keepers, and about thirty candidates on the sea ice at a time. Small, because it is a gatehouse on a rock.
places.where: Region 7, 5.7 tiles (about 140 km, some nine days' road) from the seat. On the map: a low islet of black rock in the open cold sea. A cold giao (flood-dragon) once coiled here, and its body is remembered in the great coiling ridge of pressure ice around the islet. Water 59 %, Ice 14. Băng Tâm Các's outer gate: the Beast Hall (ice beasts, the sect's mounts), the guest alchemist's hall outside the array, the stewards; the Frost Test is sat on the sea ice beside the islet until dawn.
places.imagined: Dawn after a Frost Test night. The sea around the black islet is frozen in a wide white skirt, and the old pressure ridge of ice coils three times around the islet like the body of a white serpent, its head-end lifted where it cracked last thaw. On the rock, inside a low white wall, the outer gate: long low stables for the ice beasts with steam coming from their doors, a few white halls, a courtyard where a white ice-elk is being led out. Outside the wall on a separate spur, the guest alchemist's squat stone hall with a tall chimney breathing white steam. On the sea ice beside the islet, a perfectly smooth round field of glassy blue ice where about thirty candidates sit in rows, white with frost, some slumped, while two stewards in white walk between them. Bones of old prey on the rocks.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Giao Chử, the outer gate and beast hall of Băng Tâm Các, a low rocky islet ringed by a serpent-shaped ridge of pressure ice in a cold northern sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn. The islet lies in the centre of the frame, about eight hundred metres long, pale grey-tan rock with a dark cliffed flank on its eastern end and a little thin green moss in the sheltered hollows; two more small bare rock islets sit far off at the right edge. Around it the dark blue sea is frozen in a wide white skirt about two kilometres across, and beyond the ice edge the water is open, deep and cold. Signature element: a huge ridge of pressure ice, white and glacier-blue, thick as a city wall, coils three times around the islet like the body of a giant serpent, cracked and tilted in places, with its outer end rising from the ice like a lifted head. The outer gate: on the flat southern shelf of the rock, inside a low white stone wall about two hundred metres long, stand some twenty buildings. Four long low stables for ice beasts send white steam from their doors, three white halls have grey-blue tile roofs, and a stone courtyard holds a pale ice-elk with crystal antlers being led out by a tiny figure. On a separate rocky spur outside the wall stands the guest alchemist's squat grey stone hall with a tall square chimney breathing white steam. Beside the islet lies a perfectly smooth round field of glassy pale-blue sea ice, about two hundred paces across, where some thirty tiny candidates sit cross-legged in neat rows, white with frost, a few slumped; two small figures in white walk between the rows. Bleached bones of old prey lie scattered over the black rocks of the shore. Light: the first pink-gold dawn light from the upper left, long cold blue shadows across the ice folds, breath and steam hanging in the still air.

places.name: Tuần Tùng Đường
places.size: A minor sect's seat: a palisaded oval about 150 m long on a hill crown, about 20 buildings for roughly 40 wardens and drivers. Young (founded 1191) and poor, so everything is timber and plain, scaled to a road-warden hall rather than a city.
places.where: Region 4, the temperate pine sea. On the map: rolling hills under dense dark pine forest, with grey rock outcrops breaking through the trees and a river winding at the south-east; the hall stands on a hill about 450 m high, off the road, 9 tiles above the market Tùng Hạ Thị. Wood 43 %. A young sect (founded 1191) of road wardens and wolf hunters, about 40 people: the wardens' hall, the stables, the shooting yard; the pines' riders of the Coiled Root Hall lodge here. They live on wolf pelts and the pines' bounty on wolf ears.
places.imagined: Late afternoon in early winter, the first snow on the hilltop. The hill is a bald round crown of rock and grass rising out of an endless sea of dark pines, with grey crags poking through the forest around it. On the crown, a palisade of tall sharpened pine trunks makes a rough oval. Inside: the long wardens' hall of dark timber with a steep shingle roof and smoke from two chimneys, a stable block with horses in a paddock, sheds, a smithy glowing, and the shooting yard with straw targets and a line of wardens shooting. Over the gate hangs a row of grey wolf pelts. A watch platform is built high into the one great pine that stands inside the wall. A cart track winds down through the trees toward the river and the road. A caravan of six wagons is coming up the track.
places.subject: The place: Tuần Tùng Đường, the hall of the pine wardens, a young sect of road guards and wolf hunters on a hilltop in a sea of pines. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a late afternoon in early winter. Rolling green-and-gold hills under dense dark pine forest run to the horizon, with open grassy slopes between the tree stands and grey rock outcrops breaking through the forest; a river winds in the lower right corner, catching the light. In the centre one round hill, about four hundred and fifty metres above the valleys, rises above the trees with a bare crown of grey rock and pale grass dusted with the first snow. The hall: on the crown, a rough oval palisade of tall sharpened pine trunks about one hundred and fifty metres long, with a heavy timber gate on the downhill side; over the gate hangs a long row of grey wolf pelts. Inside stand some twenty plain buildings for about forty wardens and drivers. A long wardens' hall of dark weathered timber on a stone footing has a steep shingle roof and smoke from two chimneys; a stable block opens on a paddock with a dozen horses; several sheds stand beside a small smithy with an orange glow at its door; and a bare trampled shooting yard has a row of straw targets where a line of tiny wardens loose arrows. Signature element: inside the wall stands one huge old pine, far taller than the rest, with a wooden watch platform and ladder built high into its branches. A cart track winds down the hill through the pines toward the river, and a small caravan of six covered wagons with a few riders climbs it. Nothing is ornate: no pagodas, no tiled roofs, only rough, strong, practical timber and stone. Light: low golden sun from the upper left, long blue shadows across the snow and the trees, a thin blue haze of woodsmoke over the crown.
